name: research-in-5
description: >-
  Build a "Research in 5" weekly paper review for Baylor Athletics staff: a 5-slide
  deck (dark and light), a Teams post, and a staff email from one research paper.
  Use when the user says "/research-in-5", "research in 5 on this paper", "weekly
  research review", "review this paper for the staff", "make the slides for this
  paper", "turn this study into a research review", or hands over a paper (PDF, DOI,
  article URL, or Zotero item) for the weekly series. Also use to rebuild, restyle,
  or version an existing review (#001, v2, v3). Do not use for a research-backed
  answer to a sport-science question (use sports-science-research-grounding), a
  topic education deck with no single paper (use five-slides-generator), a plain
  Zotero search (use pp-zotero-research-library), or a quick in-chat summary of a
  paper when no deck, Teams post, or email is wanted.
---

# Research in 5

The procedure, content rules, and build tooling live in the project repo, not here.
This skill gets you into the repo and carries the lessons that are easy to relearn
the hard way.

## Start

1. Project root: `~/Desktop/DEV/Weekly_Research_Review` (Windows) or
   `~/DEV/Weekly_Research_Review` (Mac). Missing on this machine:
   `gh repo clone erash11/Weekly_Research_Review` into DEV.
2. `git pull`, then read `docs/STATUS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, and
   `docs/CONTENT_SPEC.md`. Follow WORKFLOW.md step by step; it owns the process.
3. Background session: work in a worktree of that repo, open a PR, merge only when
   Eric says so.

Build and QA: `pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug -NoDrive`, read every
`dark-slideN.png` and `light-slideN.png`, then publish without `-NoDrive`.
Deliverables land in `07_EDUCATION/Research_in_5/NNN_slug/` on the Google Drive
primary storage drive.

## Gotchas

- **Check Zotero for the full text before settling for an abstract.** A new item's PDF may not be indexed yet: run `sync_zotero_library` with `include_fulltext: true`, then `get_paper` and look at `attachments`. #001 was first built from the abstract while the PDF sat in Zotero.
- **Article-in-press papers often have no public PDF.** Springer's PDF URL 404s even in Chrome. Ask Eric for the PDF or check Zotero; set `paper.full_text: false` only as a last resort and say so in the post.
- **Every number comes from the paper's tables, with a page, as reported.** Write `notes.md` first. Plot and tabulate exact values; never display a computed difference. Flag contradictions inside the paper (a conclusion stronger than its own limitations, a mislabeled table) in notes.md.
- **Slides carry one idea each; detail goes to the post.** Slide-facing fields have tight limits that build.js enforces (question 90, fact 26, summary 110, role line 70, takeaway 60, bottom line 55). Write those short first. `did.bullets`, `results.bullets`, extra limitations, and the discussion question are post-only.
- **Department names:** Athletic Performance (not strength and conditioning), Athletic Medicine (not sports medicine), Applied Performance (not sport science). build.js rejects others.
- **Baylor Bears Font has only A to Z, 0 to 9, space and `. : ! - #`.** It sets display text only; `headline` must fit that set. Section titles are caps statements because there is no `?`. Agency FB sets everything people read and has no `→`.
- **"Calibri" in the PDF font list is expected.** PowerPoint cannot embed Bears (OpenType-CFF) and draws it as outlines with a Calibri-tagged text layer. Only `Agency FB embedded: False` is a real failure. Both fonts must be installed before building on a new machine (`DEV/Baylor_Fonts`).
- **Run the humanizer skill on the audience copy before the final build.** Keep facts, pages, and limits; cut rule-of-three lists, "not X, but Y" lines, and stacked rhetorical questions.
- **Revisions get a new `version`** (outputs `_vN`) so the files Eric may already have shared stay on Drive. Only overwrite in place for a same-day correction, and say so.
- **The deck is checked against the paper before it can publish.** Step 5 runs `pwsh tools/verify.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug`; `publish.ps1` runs it again and refuses to copy anything to Drive on a real finding. Three outcomes: **VERIFY FAIL** means a claim is fabricated, contradicted, unsupported, or on the wrong page, so fix review.json and rebuild. **VERIFY PASS** may still name claims needing a human read - those are the `[REVIEW]` lines, where the model was not confident enough to decide, and you read them against notes.md. **VERIFY DEGRADED** means the check could not run at all (it needs the `TypeSafe_Sandbox` clone, its venv, and `~/.claude/typesafe.env`); it does not block, but report it like a DEGRADED image QA - the deck went out unchecked. `-SkipVerify` bypasses the gate; only use it after checking by hand, and say so.
- **publish.ps1 needs Windows PowerShell COM (installed PowerPoint) for the PDF export.** On the Mac, `node tools/build.js` still builds the pptx files and posts; export and publish from the Windows laptop.
- **Eric prefers the dark deck.** Both themes build every run; send the dark PDF first.

## Examples

```
User: "Research in 5 on this one: Saraee 2026, J Orthop Surg Res, alignment and jumper's knee"
→ cd into the repo, pull, read STATUS
→ Zotero: search, sync with full text, read every page; write notes.md
→ review.json (next number), humanizer pass, publish.ps1 -NoDrive, verify.ps1, read all PNGs
→ publish, commit on a branch, PR; send the dark PDF, teams.md, email.txt
```

```
User: "Make #001 less busy" / "use our department names" / "make a v2"
→ edit review.json or tools/build.js, bump version, rebuild both themes, QA, PR
```

---
name: research-in-5
description: >-
  Build a "Research in 5" weekly paper review for Baylor Athletics staff: a 5-slide
  deck (dark and light), a Teams post, and a staff email from one research paper.
  Use when the user says "/research-in-5", "research in 5 on this paper", "weekly
  research review", "review this paper for the staff", "make the slides for this
  paper", "turn this study into a research review", or hands over a paper (PDF, DOI,
  article URL, or Zotero item) for the weekly series. Also use to rebuild, restyle,
  or version an existing review (#001, v2, v3). Do not use for a research-backed
  answer to a sport-science question (use sports-science-research-grounding), a
  topic education deck with no single paper (use five-slides-generator), a plain
  Zotero search (use pp-zotero-research-library), or a quick in-chat summary of a
  paper when no deck, Teams post, or email is wanted.
---

# Research in 5

The procedure, content rules, and build tooling live in the project repo, not here.
This skill gets you into the repo and carries the lessons that are easy to relearn
the hard way.

## Start

1. Project root: `~/Desktop/DEV/Weekly_Research_Review` (Windows) or
   `~/DEV/Weekly_Research_Review` (Mac). Missing on this machine:
   `gh repo clone erash11/Weekly_Research_Review` into DEV.
2. `git pull`, then read `docs/STATUS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, and
   `docs/CONTENT_SPEC.md`. Follow WORKFLOW.md step by step; it owns the process.
3. Background session: work in a worktree of that repo, open a PR, merge only when
   Eric says so.

Build and QA: `pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug -NoDrive`, read every
`dark-slideN.png` and `light-slideN.png`, then publish without `-NoDrive`.
Deliverables land in `07_EDUCATION/Research_in_5/NNN_slug/` on the Google Drive
primary storage drive.

## Gotchas

- **Check Zotero for the full text before settling for an abstract.** A new item's PDF may not be indexed yet: run `sync_zotero_library` with `include_fulltext: true`, then `get_paper` and look at `attachments`. #001 was first built from the abstract while the PDF sat in Zotero.
- **Article-in-press papers often have no public PDF.** Springer's PDF URL 404s even in Chrome. Ask Eric for the PDF or check Zotero; set `paper.full_text: false` only as a last resort and say so in the post.
- **Every number comes from the paper's tables, with a page, as reported.** Write `notes.md` first. Plot and tabulate exact values; never display a computed difference. Flag contradictions inside the paper (a conclusion stronger than its own limitations, a mislabeled table) in notes.md.
- **Slides carry one idea each; detail goes to the post.** Slide-facing fields have tight limits that build.js enforces (question 90, fact 26, summary 110, role line 70, takeaway 60, bottom line 55). Write those short first. `did.bullets`, `results.bullets`, extra limitations, and the discussion question are post-only.
- **Department names:** Athletic Performance (not strength and conditioning), Athletic Medicine (not sports medicine), Applied Performance (not sport science). build.js rejects others.
- **Baylor Bears Font has only A to Z, 0 to 9, space and `. : ! - #`.** It sets display text only; `headline` must fit that set. Section titles are caps statements because there is no `?`. Agency FB sets everything people read and has no `→`.
- **"Calibri" in the PDF font list is expected.** PowerPoint cannot embed Bears (OpenType-CFF) and draws it as outlines with a Calibri-tagged text layer. Only `Agency FB embedded: False` is a real failure. Both fonts must be installed before building on a new machine (`DEV/Baylor_Fonts`).
- **Run the humanizer skill on the audience copy before the final build.** Keep facts, pages, and limits; cut rule-of-three lists, "not X, but Y" lines, and stacked rhetorical questions.
- **Revisions get a new `version`** (outputs `_vN`) so the files Eric may already have shared stay on Drive. Only overwrite in place for a same-day correction, and say so.
- **The deck is checked against the paper before it can publish.** Step 5 runs `pwsh tools/verify.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug`; `publish.ps1` runs it again and refuses to copy anything to Drive on a real finding. Three outcomes: **VERIFY FAIL** means a claim is fabricated, contradicted, unsupported, or on the wrong page, so fix review.json and rebuild. **VERIFY PASS** may still name claims needing a human read - those are the `[REVIEW]` lines, where the model was not confident enough to decide, and you read them against notes.md. **VERIFY DEGRADED** means the check could not run at all (it needs the `TypeSafe_Sandbox` clone, its venv, and `~/.claude/typesafe.env`); it does not block, but report it like a DEGRADED image QA - the deck went out unchecked. `-SkipVerify` bypasses the gate; only use it after checking by hand, and say so.
- **publish.ps1 needs Windows PowerShell COM (installed PowerPoint) for the PDF export.** On the Mac, `node tools/build.js` still builds the pptx files and posts; export and publish from the Windows laptop.
- **Eric prefers the dark deck.** Both themes build every run; send the dark PDF first.

## Examples

```
User: "Research in 5 on this one: Saraee 2026, J Orthop Surg Res, alignment and jumper's knee"
→ cd into the repo, pull, read STATUS
→ Zotero: search, sync with full text, read every page; write notes.md
→ review.json (next number), humanizer pass, publish.ps1 -NoDrive, verify.ps1, read all PNGs
→ publish, commit on a branch, PR; send the dark PDF, teams.md, email.txt
```

```
User: "Make #001 less busy" / "use our department names" / "make a v2"
→ edit review.json or tools/build.js, bump version, rebuild both themes, QA, PR
```

# ~/DEV — workspace map

Eric Rash — Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics. Sport science and
football analytics, plus the agent system that runs them.

This file is a **map, not a rulebook**. Behavior rules live in
`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Read only the index you need.

## Areas

| Area | Index | What lives there |
|---|---|---|
| Football | `FOOTBALL.md` | Game film, player analytics, CFB prediction. ~39k files — about two thirds of DEV. |
| Performance | `PERFORMANCE.md` | Athlete monitoring, testing, load, risk. GPS, force plate, VALD, DEXA, S2. |
| Research | `RESEARCH.md` | Literature, Zotero, book library, reading pipelines. |
| Platform | `PLATFORM.md` | KeystoneOS, dashboards, CLIs, scheduled jobs. |
| Program | `PROGRAM.md` | Staff reporting, curriculum, proposals, vetting, brand. |
| Personal | `PERSONAL.md` | Side projects. Not Baylor work. |
| Commands | `COMMANDS.md` | Desk reference: every report/project command Eric can run himself. |

## Elsewhere on disk

`~/DEV` in this file means the workspace root: `~/DEV` on the Mac,
`~/Desktop/DEV` on Windows. Paths that differ per machine are in `~/.claude/machine.md`.

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|

| SecondBrain vault | Obsidian vault, ~850 notes. Own `CLAUDE.md`. Mac `~/SecondBrain`, Windows `~/Desktop/SecondBrain`. |

## Layout rules

Full rules — grouping depth, the depth-2 discovery limit, and the gitignored-subtree
trap — live in project memory: `project_dev-layout-and-discovery.md`.

## Handling care

- `DexaProject/` holds identifiable health data. It lives on Google Drive, not in

When a file moves or a new project starts, **update the router in the same
turn**. A stale pointer is worse than no pointer.

The counts above are approximate on purpose — they convey scale, not state, and
a `~` keeps ordinary growth from making this file wrong. Re-measure them only
when one is off by enough to change a decision. Counts last checked 2026-10-02.

entries.name: TaskList
entries.description:
Use this tool to list all tasks in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

- To see what tasks are available to work on (status: 'pending', no owner, not blocked)
- To check overall progress on the project
- To find tasks that are blocked and need dependencies resolved
- After completing a task, to check for newly unblocked work or claim the next available task
- **Prefer working on tasks in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple tasks are available, as earlier tasks often set up context for later ones

## Output

Returns a summary of each task:
- **id**: Task identifier (use with TaskGet, TaskUpdate)
- **subject**: Brief description of the task
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'
- **owner**: Agent ID if assigned, empty if available
- **blockedBy**: List of open task IDs that must be resolved first (tasks with blockedBy cannot be claimed until dependencies resolve)

Use TaskGet with a specific task ID to view full details including description and comments.

entries.name: TaskStop
entries.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID ("name@team") or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.
